extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary result text, figure captions, supplementary figure captions, and OA package figures; phenotypic biofilm/in vivo findings are not promoted to direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: lcCCL28-25 damages/permeabilizes S. aureus membranes in a direct SYTOX green uptake assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct membrane-permeability support is strongest for S. aureus; no intracellular molecular target is established.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: lcCCL28-25-treated E. coli and S. aureus show membrane-associated fluorescence and microscopy morphology consistent with membrane disruption.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: lcCCL28-25 against E. coli ATCC 25922 and S. aureus ATCC 25923
mechanism_claims.limitations: For E. coli, the paper explicitly leaves open whether membrane damage is decisive or downstream; do not overclaim a sole mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: lcCCL28-25 has antibiofilm activity against P. aeruginosa FRD1, but this is phenotypic activity evidence rather than a direct molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: lcCCL28-25 and comparison peptides in P. aeruginosa FRD1 biofilm assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm inhibition/eradication is preserved as activity evidence; no biofilm-specific molecular target is assigned.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The in vivo mouse thigh infection result supports protective antibacterial activity but does not define a mechanism, and the paper notes immune-stimulation uncertainty.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: lcCCL28-25 in neutropenic mouse thigh S. aureus USA300 model

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=7:FIG 7; pdf_text:in vivo and discussion paragraphs

mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct host immune mechanism is curated from this paper.
